subproblems.title: Coordinates, distance to the plane and the cylinder of an orthonormal frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P = Eucl P, Q := span τ, let p : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map with p(y)_i = ⟪τ_i, y⟫ for all y and i, and let d : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy d(y) = ‖y − Σ_i ⟪τ_i, y⟫ τ_i‖ for all y. Put W′ := {y : ‖p(y)‖ < 1 and d(y) < 3/4}. Then: (a) d is 1-Lipschitz; (b) ‖y‖² = ‖p(y)‖² + d(y)² for all y; (c) the operator norm of p is ≤ 1; (d) p(Σ_i a_i τ_i) = a for every a ∈ ℝⁿ; (e) p(τ_i) = e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for every i; (f) d(z) = 0 for every z ∈ Q; (g) W′ ⊂⊂ B_2(0) ⊆ ℝ^P, i.e. W′ is open and closure W′ is compact and contained in B_2(0); (h) for every real γ < 3/4 and every compact K ⊆ B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ, the set K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ} is compact and K′ ⊆ W′.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (p : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl n) (d : Eucl P → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ y i, p y i = inner ℝ (τ i) y) → (∀ y, d y = ‖y - ∑ i, inner ℝ (τ i) y • τ i‖) → LipschitzWith 1 d ∧ (∀ y, ‖y‖ ^ 2 = ‖p y‖ ^ 2 + d y ^ 2) ∧ ‖p‖ ≤ 1 ∧ (∀ a : Eucl n, p (∑ i, a i • τ i) = a) ∧ (∀ i, p (τ i) = EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) ∧ (∀ z ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ), d z = 0) ∧ CompactlyContainedOpen {y : Eucl P | ‖p y‖ < 1 ∧ d y < 3 / 4} (ball (0 : Eucl P) 2) ∧ ∀ γ : ℝ, γ < 3 / 4 → ∀ K : Set (Eucl n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ ball (0 : Eucl n) 1 → IsCompact (p ⁻¹' K ∩ {y | d y ≤ γ}) ∧ p ⁻¹' K ∩ {y | d y ≤ γ} ⊆ {y : Eucl P | ‖p y‖ < 1 ∧ d y < 3 / 4}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 0 ((0a), (0b), (0d)) of the parent proof, specialized to the stated hypotheses on p and d.

Notation. For y ∈ ℝ^P put π(y) := Σ_i ⟪τ_i, y⟫ τ_i, so that d(y) = ‖y − π(y)‖ by hypothesis.

1. Inner products with the frame. By orthonormality, ⟪τ_j, Σ_i c_i τ_i⟫ = c_j for every c : Fin n → ℝ and every j (Mathlib Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). With c_i := ⟪τ_i, y⟫ this gives ⟪τ_j, π(y)⟫ = ⟪τ_j, y⟫ for all j and y.

2. Orthogonality. By linearity of the inner product in the first slot, ⟪π(y), y − π(y)⟫ = Σ_i ⟪τ_i, y⟫ (⟪τ_i, y⟫ − ⟪τ_i, π(y)⟫) = 0 by step 1.

3. Proof of (b). Orthonormality gives ‖π(y)‖² = ⟪π(y), π(y)⟫ = Σ_i ⟪τ_i, y⟫² (Orthonormal.inner_sum). Since p(y)_i = ⟪τ_i, y⟫, also ‖p(y)‖² = Σ_i p(y)_i² = Σ_i ⟪τ_i, y⟫² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). Writing y = π(y) + (y − π(y)) with orthogonal summands (step 2), Pythagoras (norm_add_sq_eq_norm_sq_add_norm_sq_real) yields ‖y‖² = ‖π(y)‖² + ‖y − π(y)‖² = ‖p(y)‖² + d(y)².

4. Consequences. d(y) = ‖y − π(y)‖ ≥ 0, and by (b): d(y) ≤ ‖y‖ and ‖p(y)‖ ≤ ‖y‖ for all y. The latter gives (c) by ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound with constant 1.

5. Proof of (a). π is additive: π(x − y) = π(x) − π(y) (inner_sub_right, sub_smul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib). Hence x − π(x) = (y − π(y)) + ((x − y) − π(x − y)), and the triangle inequality with step 4 gives d(x) ≤ d(y) + d(x − y) ≤ d(y) + ‖x − y‖ = d(y) + dist(x, y) for all x, y. By LipschitzWith.of_le_add, d is 1-Lipschitz; in particular d is continuous.

6. Proof of (d). For a ∈ ℝⁿ and each j, p(Σ_i a_i τ_i)_j = ⟪τ_j, Σ_i a_i τ_i⟫ = a_j by step 1; by extensionality of vectors in ℝⁿ, p(Σ_i a_i τ_i) = a.

7. Proof of (e). p(τ_i)_j = ⟪τ_j, τ_i⟫, which is 1 if j = i and 0 otherwise (orthonormal_iff_ite); this is the j-th coordinate of EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Hence p(τ_i) = e_i.

8. Proof of (f). If z ∈ Q = span(range τ), then z = Σ_i c_i τ_i for some c : Fin n → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). By step 1, ⟪τ_i, z⟫ = c_i, so π(z) = Σ_i c_i τ_i = z and d(z) = ‖z − z‖ = 0.

9. Proof of (g). The functions y ↦ ‖p(y)‖ and d are continuous (p is continuous; step 5), so W′ = {‖p(·)‖ < 1} ∩ {d < 3/4} is open (isOpen_lt). The set F := {y : ‖p(y)‖ ≤ 1 and d(y) ≤ 3/4} is closed (isClosed_le) and contains W′, so closure W′ ⊆ F (closure_minimal). For y ∈ F, (b) and 0 ≤ d(y) ≤ 3/4 give ‖y‖² ≤ 1 + 9/16 = 25/16, so ‖y‖ ≤ 5/4. Hence closure W′ ⊆ closedBall(0, 5/4) ⊆ B_2(0), and closure W′ is compact, being a closed subset of the compact ball closedBall(0, 5/4) (isCompact_closedBall, IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). So W′ ⊂⊂ B_2(0).

10. Proof of (h). Let γ < 3/4 and K ⊆ B_1(0) be compact. If y ∈ K′ then p(y) ∈ K ⊆ B_1(0), so ‖p(y)‖ < 1, and d(y) ≤ γ < 3/4; hence K′ ⊆ W′. Moreover, by (b) and 0 ≤ d(y) < 3/4, ‖y‖² < 1 + 9/16, so K′ ⊆ closedBall(0, 5/4). K′ is closed: K is closed (compact in a Hausdorff space), p is continuous, and {d ≤ γ} is closed since d is continuous. Therefore K′ is compact as a closed subset of the compact ball closedBall(0, 5/4). ∎
proof_key_steps: π(y) := Σ⟪τ_i,y⟫τ_i satisfies ⟪τ_j, π(y)⟫ = ⟪τ_j, y⟫, hence y − π(y) ⊥ π(y).
Pythagoras with ‖π(y)‖² = Σ⟪τ_i,y⟫² = ‖p(y)‖² gives ‖y‖² = ‖p(y)‖² + d(y)²; hence d(y) ≤ ‖y‖ and ‖p‖ ≤ 1.
Additivity of π and d(u) ≤ ‖u‖ give d(x) ≤ d(y) + dist(x, y), so d is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_le_add).
Orthonormality gives p(Σ a_iτ_i) = a, p(τ_i) = e_i, and π = id on span τ, so d = 0 on Q.
closure W′ ⊆ {‖p‖ ≤ 1, d ≤ 3/4} ⊆ closedBall(0, 5/4) ⊆ B_2(0), so W′ ⊂⊂ B_2(0).
K′ = p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ} is closed, contained in closedBall(0, 5/4) and in W′, hence compact.

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure on the span of an orthonormal frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, τ : Fin n → ℝ^P orthonormal, Q := span τ ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, and ι(a) := Σ_i a_i τ_i for a ∈ ℝⁿ = Eucl n, with Lebesgue measure da = volume on ℝⁿ. Then (i) ∫_Q h dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(ι(a)) da for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ, and (ii) (Hⁿ⌞Q)(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ h : Eucl P → ℝ, ∫ z in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Eucl P)), h z ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) = ∫ a : Eucl n, h (∑ i, a i • τ i)) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Eucl P))) K < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (0c) of the parent proof.

1. ι is an isometry. ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is linear. By orthonormality, ‖ι(a)‖² = ⟪Σ_i a_i τ_i, Σ_i a_i τ_i⟫ = Σ_i a_i² (Orthonormal.inner_sum) = ‖a‖² (EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq). Hence ‖ι(a)‖ = ‖a‖ for all a, and since ι is additive, dist(ι a, ι b) = ‖ι(a − b)‖ = ‖a − b‖; so ι is an isometry (AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm applied to the linear map ι).

2. range ι = Q. A vector z lies in span(range τ) iff z = Σ_i c_i τ_i for some c : Fin n → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Given such c, the vector a := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ).symm c ∈ ℝⁿ has coordinates c_i, so ι(a) = z; conversely every ι(a) is of this form with c_i := a_i.

3. Image measure. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure (an isometry pushes μHE[n] forward to μHE[n] restricted to its range), (μHE[n] on ℝⁿ).map ι = μHE[n].restrict(range ι) = Hⁿ⌞Q by step 2. By EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, μHE[n] on ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) equals Lebesgue measure. Hence volume.map ι = Hⁿ⌞Q.

4. Proof of (i). An isometry from the complete space ℝⁿ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a measurable embedding (IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). For a measurable embedding the change of variables ∫ h d(volume.map ι) = ∫ h(ι(a)) da holds for every function h, measurable or not (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). With step 3, ∫_Q h dHⁿ = ∫ h d(Hⁿ⌞Q) = ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(ι(a)) da.

5. Proof of (ii). Let K be compact; it is closed, hence measurable. By step 3 and Measure.map_apply, (Hⁿ⌞Q)(K) = volume(ι⁻¹(K)). Since ι is a closed embedding, ι⁻¹(K) is compact (IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage), and Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). Hence (Hⁿ⌞Q)(K) < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(a) = Σ a_iτ_i is a linear isometry ℝⁿ → ℝ^P by orthonormality.
range ι = span τ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume give volume.map ι = Hⁿ⌞Q.
ι is a closed, hence measurable, embedding; MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives (i).
Measure.map_apply and compactness of ι⁻¹(K) give (ii).

subproblems.title: The current of a constant n-vector against a measure finite on compacts
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and w ∈ NVector(ℝ^P, n) (a continuous linear functional on n-covectors). Then there is a current T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) such that (μ, x ↦ w) is a measure representation of T (IsMeasureRepresentation T μ (fun _ => w)): for every ω ∈ D^n(U), x ↦ w(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ w(ω(x)) dμ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n), (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsMeasureRepresentation T μ (fun _ => w)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (1a)–(1c) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary measure finite on compacts and a constant n-vector.

1. Integrability. μ is finite on compact sets (an IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts instance built from the hypothesis). Let ω ∈ D^n(U): ω is C^∞ with compact support. The function f_ω(x) := w(ω(x)) is continuous (w is a continuous linear map and ω is continuous) and has compact support, because w(0) = 0 (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). A continuous compactly supported function is integrable for a measure finite on compacts (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). So f_ω is μ-integrable.

2. Linearity. Define L(ω) := ∫ f_ω dμ for ω ∈ D^n(U). Since forms add and scale pointwise and w is linear, f_{ω+η} = f_ω + f_η and f_{rω} = r·f_ω. By step 1 and integral_add, L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η); by integral_const_mul, L(rω) = r·L(ω). So L is a linear functional on D^n(U).

3. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in D^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for every j, and the 0-th iterated derivatives of ω_j converge uniformly on K to the 0-th iterated derivative of the zero form, which is 0. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every r > 0 we have ‖ω_j(x)‖ < r for all x ∈ K and all large j. Let ε > 0, put m_K := (μ(K)).toReal (finite by hypothesis) and C := ‖w‖·m_K + 1 > 0, and take j so large that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/C for all x ∈ K. Since tsupport ω_j ⊆ K, ω_j(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so f_{ω_j} vanishes off K and ∫ f_{ω_j} dμ = ∫_K f_{ω_j} dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). For x ∈ K, |f_{ω_j}(x)| ≤ ‖w‖·‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ‖w‖·ε/C (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). Hence (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, μ(K) < ∞) |L(ω_j)| ≤ ‖w‖·(ε/C)·m_K = ε·(‖w‖·m_K)/C < ε. Thus L(ω_j) → 0.

4. Conclusion. T := (L, step 3) is a GeometricCurrentOn U n. By definition T(ω) = ∫ w(ω(x)) dμ(x), and the integrand is μ-integrable by step 1; this is exactly IsMeasureRepresentation T μ (fun _ => w). ∎
proof_key_steps: For ω ∈ D^n(U), x ↦ w(ω(x)) is continuous with compact support, hence μ-integrable.
L(ω) := ∫ w(ω) dμ is linear (integral_add, integral_const_mul).
If ω_j → 0 in D^n(U), supports lie in one compact K and sup_K ‖ω_j‖ → 0, so |L(ω_j)| ≤ ‖w‖·μ(K)·sup_K‖ω_j‖ → 0.
T := (L, continuity) is a current and (μ, const w) represents it by construction.

subproblems.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to an open set
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P and A ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let X, R ∈ D_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) with X integer multiplicity and R a restriction of X to A (IsRestriction X A R). Then R is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U A : Set (Eucl P)) (X R : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsOpen U → IsOpen A → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsRestriction X A R → IsIntegerMultiplicity R
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (6d) and (7a) of the parent proof (“the same argument with the open set A_γ shows that R_k = τ(M′_k ∩ A_γ, θ′_k, ξ′_k) is i.m.”), stated for an arbitrary open set A.

1. Data. Since X is integer multiplicity there are M, θ, ξ such that (M, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in U of dimension k (IsRectifiableTriple U k M θ ξ), θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M, and X(ω) = tauAction(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ for every ω ∈ D^k(U).

2. Formula for R. By the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.polyhedral_approx_restriction_tau (U open), every restriction R of X to a set A satisfies R(ω) = tauAction(M ∩ A, θ, ξ)(ω) for all ω ∈ D^k(U). (Not needed; an alternative route: (Hᵏ⌞M, θξ) is a measure representation of X, with integrability from Submission.ltg_tau_integrable; R is given by some representation (μ₁, v₁) of X; Submission.slicing_representation_unique with W := U shows that both representations have the same integral over the measurable set A, and ∫_A θξ(ω) d(Hᵏ⌞M) = tauAction(M ∩ A, θ, ξ)(ω).)

3. (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) is a rectifiable triple in U. A is open, hence measurable.
 - subset: M ∩ A ⊆ M ⊆ U.
 - null-measurability: M is Hᵏ-null-measurable and A is measurable, so M ∩ A is Hᵏ-null-measurable.
 - countable k-rectifiability: M ∩ A ⊆ M (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
 - positivity: θ > 0 on M ∩ A ⊆ M.
 - local integrability: for compact K ⊆ U, θ is Hᵏ-integrable on M ∩ K, hence on the subset (M ∩ A) ∩ K (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
 - measurability of ξ: ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M, hence for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A) ≤ Hᵏ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono).
 - orientation: the orients property of (M, θ, ξ) holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e., hence Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset), and Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ A (ae_restrict_mem₀). Fix such an x, together with an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P such that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ. The symmetric difference of M and M ∩ A is M ∖ A, which does not meet A, so Hᵏ(symmDiff M (M ∩ A) ∩ A) = Hᵏ(∅) = 0. A is open and contains x, and θ′ := θ agrees with θ everywhere. Hence the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr (with V := A, M′ := M ∩ A, θ′ := θ, L := span τ) gives HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M ∩ A) θ x (span τ). With the same τ and the same sign of ξ(x), the orients property of (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) holds at x.

4. Integrality. θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M ∩ A, since M ∩ A ⊆ M.

5. Conclusion. By steps 2–4, (M ∩ A, θ, ξ) witnesses IsIntegerMultiplicity R. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write X = τ(M, θ, ξ) with integer θ.
Submission.polyhedral_approx_restriction_tau gives R = τ(M ∩ A, θ, ξ) on D^k(U).
(M ∩ A, θ, ξ) inherits subset, null-measurability, rectifiability, positivity, local integrability and measurability.
Orientation: (M ∖ A) ∩ A = ∅ and A is open, so Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr transfers the weighted tangent planes of (M, θ) to (M ∩ A, θ).
θ is integer-valued on M ∩ A, so R is integer multiplicity.

Source: Steps 3, 4, 5, (5d), (6b) and (6c) of the parent proof (printed Proof of 8.2, display (8) and the selection argument “by 4.5(1) and a selection argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2”), with U, W, d, L, a, b general.

Conventions. (R1) and (R2) are the uniqueness and mass-measure/restriction parts of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory. For s ∈ ℝ put A_s := {x ∈ U : d(x) < s}. W is open, W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U, and d is continuous (Lipschitz).

1. Mass measures. For each k, X_k has finite mass on every V ⊂⊂ U, so (R2) gives a measure μ_k with IsMassMeasure X_k μ_k, a restriction of X_k to every measurable set, and M_V(S) = μ_k(V ∩ A) for every restriction S of X_k to a set A and every open V ⊆ U. Consequently, for every restriction S of X_k to any set A,
 (∗) M_W(S) = μ_k(W ∩ A) ≤ μ_k(W) = M_W(X_k),
 the last equality because W ⊂⊂ U and μ_k is a mass measure of X_k.

2. Slicing. The zero current has M_V(0) = 0 for every V (each admissible value is ofReal 0 = 0). Hence, for each k, T := X_k satisfies the hypothesis of SlicingTheorem on U (M_V(X_k) < ∞ and M_V(∂X_k) = M_V(0) = 0 < ∞ for V ⊂⊂ U), and d is L-Lipschitz on U. Let S^k_t ∈ D_m(U) (t ∈ ℝ) be the slices it provides.

3. Slices are boundaries. Fix k and t. IsSlice X_k d t S^k_t gives currents A′ and B′ with A′ a restriction of X_k to A_t, B′ a restriction of ∂X_k = 0 to A_t, and S^k_t(ω) = ∂A′(ω) − B′(ω) for all ω. The set A_t is measurable (first component of B′'s IsRestriction), and the zero current is a restriction of the zero current to A_t: use the representation μ := 0, v := 0, for which all integrals vanish. By (R1), B′ = 0, hence S^k_t = ∂A′. Choose such an A′ =: A^k_t for all k and t; thus A^k_t is a restriction of X_k to A_t with ∂A^k_t = S^k_t.

4. Slice mass bound. By Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz, ‖fderiv ℝ d x‖ ≤ L for every x, so the a.e. derivative hypothesis of the slicing mass clause holds on W with L_W := L. The band {x ∈ U : a < d(x) < b} is open, hence measurable, so by step 1 there is a restriction Rb_k of X_k to it. The slicing mass clause (with W, L, a < b, Rb_k) gives a measurable g_k : ℝ → [0, ∞] with M_W(S^k_t) ≤ g_k(t) for all t ∈ (a, b) and
 ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g_k ≤ L · M_W(Rb_k) ≤ L · M_W(X_k) ≤ L · C₀, where C₀ := sup_j M_W(X_j) < ∞, using (∗).

5. Restriction limits. Apply (RWL) to U, the sequence (X_k), X, W and φ := d: X_k ⇀ X, W is open and W ⊆ U, sup_k M_W(X_k) < ∞, and d is continuous on U. It gives a strictly increasing ψ and a countable E ⊆ ℝ such that for every s ∉ E, all restrictions R′_j of X_{ψ(j)} to A_s (j ∈ ℕ) and every restriction R of X to A_s, R′_j(ω) → R(ω) for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

6. Fatou. F(t) := liminf_k g_{ψ(k)}(t) is measurable (Measurable.liminf), and by Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le) ∫⁻_{(a,b)} F ≤ liminf_k ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g_{ψ(k)} ≤ L · C₀ < ∞ (liminf_le_of_frequently_le' with the bound of step 4 for every k). Hence F(t) < ∞ for (volume⌞(a,b))-a.e. t (ae_lt_top).

7. Choice of γ. E is countable, hence Lebesgue-null, so a.e. t satisfies t ∉ E (also for volume⌞(a,b)); and (volume⌞(a,b))-a.e. t lies in (a, b) (ae_restrict_mem). Since volume((a, b)) = b − a > 0, the measure volume⌞(a,b) is nonzero, so its a.e. filter is nontrivial (ae_neBot) and a property holding a.e. holds for some t. Hence there is γ ∈ (a, b) ∖ E with F(γ) < ∞.

8. Subsequence. Put G := F(γ) + 1 < ∞. Since liminf_k g_{ψ(k)}(γ) = F(γ) < G, infinitely many k satisfy g_{ψ(k)}(γ) < G (frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt), so there is a strictly increasing σ with g_{ψ(σ(k))}(γ) < G for all k (extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Let κ := ψ ∘ σ (strictly increasing) and R_k := A^{κ(k)}_γ.

9. Verification.
 - R_k is a restriction of X_{κ(k)} to A_γ by step 3.
 - M_W(R_k) ≤ M_W(X_{κ(k)}) by (∗).
 - ∂R_k = S^{κ(k)}_γ by step 3, so M_W(∂R_k) ≤ g_{κ(k)}(γ) < G by step 4 (γ ∈ (a, b)) and step 8.
 - Let R be a restriction of X to A_γ and ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Step 5 with s := γ ∉ E and R′_j := A^{ψ(j)}_γ (a restriction of X_{ψ(j)} to A_γ by step 3) gives R′_j(ω) → R(ω). Since σ is strictly increasing, σ(k) → ∞, so R_k(ω) = R′_{σ(k)}(ω) → R(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: (R2) of Submission.iwl_restriction_theory gives mass measures μ_k; every restriction S of X_k satisfies M_W(S) = μ_k(W ∩ A) ≤ M_W(X_k).
SlicingTheorem applies to each cycle X_k (∂X_k = 0 has zero mass); by (R1) the boundary restriction vanishes, so slices are S^k_t = ∂A^k_t with A^k_t a restriction of X_k to {d < t}.
Slicing mass clause with ‖Dd‖ ≤ L: measurable g_k with M_W(S^k_t) ≤ g_k(t) on (a, b) and ∫⁻ g_k ≤ L·sup_j M_W(X_j).
(RWL) gives ψ and a countable exceptional set E.
Fatou: liminf_k g_{ψ(k)} has finite integral, so it is finite at some γ ∈ (a, b) ∖ E.
Extract σ with g_{ψσ(k)}(γ) < G; set κ := ψ∘σ, R_k := A^{κ(k)}_γ.
Verify the restriction, mass, boundary-mass and convergence claims; convergence passes to the subsequence σ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1, 2, 3–7 of the parent proof (printed Proof of 8.2, displays (8)–(9): η_{x,λ_j#}T_{j′} ⌞ {d < γ}, localized to the cylinder), with the sibling lemmas frame_geometry, span_integral, const_vector_current, slice_selection and restriction_open_im.

Notation. B := B_2(0) ⊆ ℝ^P, C₀ := sup_k M_B(Y_k) < ∞, μ_Q := Hⁿ⌞Q. For a current T ∈ D_k(U′) and W₀ ⊆ U′, T|_{W₀} := T.restrictDomain (T|_{W₀}(ω) = T(ω) for ω ∈ D^k(W₀) regarded in D^k(U′) via testFormOnInclusion).

0. Geometry and measure. By frame_geometry: d is 1-Lipschitz (so continuous), d = 0 on Q, and W′ ⊂⊂ B; in particular W′ is open and W′ ⊆ closure W′ ⊆ B. By span_integral (ii), μ_Q(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Q is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and measurable.

1. The limit current. Apply const_vector_current with U := B, μ := μ_Q and w := c·simpleNVector τ. It gives X ∈ D_n(B) with IsMeasureRepresentation X μ_Q (const w). Since (c·simpleNVector τ)(α) = c·α(τ) (simpleNVector_apply), integral_const_mul gives X(ω) = c∫_Q ω(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) for every ω ∈ D^n(B).

2. Two facts on restrictDomain. Let T ∈ D_k(U′) and W₀ ⊆ U′.
 (a) M_V(T|_{W₀}) ≤ M_V(T) for every set V: an admissible form ω for M_V(T|_{W₀}) (ω ∈ D^k(W₀), tsupport ω ⊆ V, Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1 everywhere) is, regarded in D^k(U′), admissible for M_V(T) with the same value T(ω) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn); take the supremum.
 (b) If k = j + 1 then ∂(T|_{W₀}) = (∂T)|_{W₀}: for ω ∈ D^j(W₀) both sides equal T applied to the form dω, because the inclusion D(W₀) → D(U′) does not change the underlying form and commutes with exterior differentiation.

3. The currents X_k := Y_k|_B ∈ D_n(B).
 - X_k is integer multiplicity by the comparator-accepted Submission.br_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (B open).
 - ∂X_k = (∂Y_k)|_B = 0 by 2(b).
 - For V ⊆ B: M_V(X_k) ≤ M_V(Y_k) ≤ M_B(Y_k) ≤ C₀ by 2(a) and monotonicity of massOn. Hence M_V(X_k) < ∞ for every V ⊂⊂ B (V ⊆ closure V ⊆ B), and sup_k M_{W′}(X_k) ≤ C₀ < ∞.
 - X_k ⇀ X in B: for ω ∈ D^n(B), regarded in D^n(ℝ^P) it has tsupport ω ⊆ B, so X_k(ω) = Y_k(ω) → c∫_Q ω(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) = X(ω) by hypothesis and step 1.

4. Slice selection. Apply slice_selection (with SlicingTheorem and (RWL)) to U := B, W := W′, the sequence (X_k), X, d, L := 1, a := 1/4, b := 1/2; its hypotheses were checked in steps 0 and 3. It gives γ ∈ (1/4, 1/2), a strictly increasing κ, currents R_k ∈ D_n(B) and G < ∞ such that: R_k is a restriction of X_{κ(k)} to A_γ := {x ∈ B : d(x) < γ}; M_{W′}(R_k) ≤ M_{W′}(X_{κ(k)}); M_{W′}(∂R_k) ≤ G; and R_k(ω) → R(ω) for every restriction R of X to A_γ and every ω ∈ D^n(B) with tsupport ω ⊆ W′. In particular 0 ≤ γ < 3/4.

5. X is a restriction of itself to A_γ (parent (6a)). A_γ = B ∩ {d < γ} is open, hence measurable. Use the representation (μ_Q, const w) of step 1. For ω ∈ D^n(B), the function f(x) := w(ω(x)) vanishes at every x ∈ Q ∖ A_γ: such x has d(x) = 0 < γ (step 0), hence x ∉ B ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and f(x) = 0. Since μ_Q-a.e. x lies in Q (ae_restrict_iff' with Q measurable), f = 0 μ_Q-a.e. off A_γ, and setIntegral_eq_integral_of_ae_compl_eq_zero gives ∫_{A_γ} f dμ_Q = ∫ f dμ_Q = X(ω). Hence IsRestriction X A_γ X, and by step 4, R_k(ω) → X(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(B) with tsupport ω ⊆ W′.

6. R_k is integer multiplicity, by restriction_open_im applied to the open sets B and A_γ, the integer multiplicity current X_{κ(k)} and its restriction R_k.

7. Localization. Let Z_k := R_k|_{W′} ∈ D_n(W′) (W′ ⊆ B).
 (a) Z_k is integer multiplicity by Submission.br_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (W′ open) and step 6.
 (b) Mass: M(Z_k) = M_{W′}(Z_k) ≤ M_{W′}(R_k) ≤ M_{W′}(X_{κ(k)}) ≤ sup_j M_{W′}(X_j) by 2(a) and step 4.
 (c) Boundary mass: ∂Z_k = (∂R_k)|_{W′} by 2(b), so M(∂Z_k) ≤ M_{W′}(∂R_k) ≤ G by 2(a) and step 4.
 Hence sup_k (M(Z_k) + M(∂Z_k)) ≤ sup_j M_{W′}(X_j) + G < ∞ (step 3 and G < ∞).
 (d) Convergence: for ω ∈ D^n(W′), regarded in D^n(B) it has tsupport ω ⊆ W′, so Z_k(ω) = R_k(ω) → X(ω) = c∫_Q ω(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) by steps 5 and 1.
 (e) Support: spt Z_k = W′ ∖ zeroRegion(Z_k). Suppose y ∈ spt Z_k and d(y) > γ. The set O := W′ ∩ {d > γ} is open (d continuous) and contains y, so B_ε(y) ⊆ O for some ε > 0. Put D := B_{ε/2}(y). Then D is open, closure D ⊆ closedBall(y, ε/2) ⊆ B_ε(y) ⊆ O ⊆ W′, and closure D is compact (closed subset of a closed ball). Z_k vanishes on D: let ω ∈ D^n(W′) with tsupport ω ⊆ D. Since R_k is a restriction of X_{κ(k)} to A_γ, there is a representation (μ, v) of X_{κ(k)} with R_k(ω) = ∫_{A_γ} v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). Every x ∈ A_γ has d(x) < γ, hence x ∉ O ⊇ tsupport ω, so ω(x) = 0 and v(x)(ω(x)) = 0; thus Z_k(ω) = R_k(ω) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). Therefore D belongs to the family of relatively compact open sets whose union is zeroRegion(Z_k), so y ∈ D ⊆ zeroRegion(Z_k), contradicting y ∈ spt Z_k. Hence spt Z_k ⊆ {d ≤ γ}.

8. Conclusion. γ (with 0 ≤ γ < 3/4) and the currents Z_k satisfy all four requirements by 7(a), 7(e), 7(b)–(c) and 7(d). ∎
proof_key_steps: frame_geometry: d 1-Lipschitz, d = 0 on Q, W′ ⊂⊂ B_2(0); span_integral: Hⁿ⌞Q finite on compacts.
const_vector_current gives X = c[[Q]] ∈ D_n(B) with representation (Hⁿ⌞Q, c·simpleNVector τ).
X_k := Y_k|_B are i.m. cycles with M_V(X_k) ≤ C₀ and X_k ⇀ X (restrictDomain lowers mass and commutes with ∂).
slice_selection on (B, W′, d, 1/4, 1/2) gives γ ∈ (1/4,1/2), κ, restrictions R_k of X_{κ(k)} to {d < γ}, mass and boundary-mass bounds, convergence to restrictions of X.
X is a restriction of itself to {d < γ} (its measure lives on Q, where d = 0), so R_k → X on forms supported in W′.
restriction_open_im: R_k is i.m.; Z_k := R_k|_{W′} is i.m. with bounded M + M(∂) and Z_k ⇀ c[[Q]]|_{W′}.
Restrictions vanish on forms supported off {d < γ}, so spt Z_k ⊆ {d ≤ γ}.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 8 and 9 of the parent proof (printed Proof of 8.2: p_#S̃_j ∈ D_n(B_1ⁿ(0)), the mass identities (10), and p_#S̃_j ⇀ θ(x)p_#[[ℝⁿ × {0}]] = θ(x)[[ℝⁿ]]), with the sibling lemmas frame_geometry and span_integral.

0. Geometry. By frame_geometry: W′ ⊂⊂ B_2(0), in particular W′ is open; ‖p‖ ≤ 1; p(Σ_i a_i τ_i) = a for a ∈ ℝⁿ; p(τ_i) = e_i; d = 0 on Q; and for every compact K ⊆ V the set K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ} is compact and K′ ⊆ W′. Since p is continuous linear, it is C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff) with fderiv ℝ p x = p for every x (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv), so ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ ≤ 1. Also p(W′) ⊆ V, because ‖p(y)‖ < 1 for y ∈ W′. Q is closed, hence measurable.

1. Properness. Fix k and a compact K ⊆ V. Since spt Z_k = W′ ∖ zeroRegion(Z_k) ⊆ {d ≤ γ} and K′ ⊆ W′, we have p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt Z_k = K′ ∖ zeroRegion(Z_k): a point of the left side lies in p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ} and outside the zero region; conversely a point of K′ outside the zero region lies in W′, hence in spt Z_k. As zeroRegion(Z_k) is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion), K′ ∖ zeroRegion(Z_k) is a closed subset of the compact set K′, hence compact (IsCompact.diff).

2. Push-forward. For each k apply (SPF), with LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity, to U := W′, V, X := Z_k (integer multiplicity) and f := p; the hypotheses (W′, V open, p C^∞, p(W′) ⊆ V, properness) hold by steps 0–1. Choosing for every k (axiom of choice) the current it provides, we get integer multiplicity S′_k ∈ D_n(V) such that
 (a) S′_k(ω) = Z_k(η) whenever ω ∈ D^n(V), η ∈ D^n(W′) and η(x) = ω(p(x))∘(fderiv ℝ p x) for all x in some open N ⊇ spt Z_k;
 (b) instantiating the ∀ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c → … clause of (SPF) at the constant 1 (allowed since ‖fderiv ℝ p x‖ ≤ 1; this 1 is unrelated to the constant c of the statement), for every W″ ⊆ ℝⁿ: M_{W″}(S′_k) ≤ ofReal(1^n)·M_{p⁻¹(W″) ∩ W′}(Z_k) ≤ M_{W′}(Z_k) = M(Z_k) and M_{W″}(∂S′_k) ≤ ofReal(1^m)·M_{p⁻¹(W″) ∩ W′}(∂Z_k) ≤ M(∂Z_k) (massOn_mono).

3. Mass bound. By 2(b), for every W″ ⊂⊂ V: sup_k (M_{W″}(S′_k) + M_{W″}(∂S′_k)) ≤ sup_k (M(Z_k) + M(∂Z_k)) < ∞.

4. Cutoff (smooth Urysohn). Fix ω ∈ D^n(V) and put K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of V, and K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ}, compact with K′ ⊆ W′ (step 0, using γ < 3/4). Choose δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K′ ⊆ W′ (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). The closed sets s := (thickening δ₀ K′)ᶜ and t := cthickening (δ₀/2) K′ are disjoint (cthickening_subset_thickening'), so by exists_contDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed there is a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with ζ(x) = 0 ⇔ x ∈ s and ζ(x) = 1 ⇔ x ∈ t. Then support ζ ⊆ thickening δ₀ K′, so tsupport ζ ⊆ closure(thickening δ₀ K′) ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K′ ⊆ W′ (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening), and ζ has compact support since cthickening δ₀ K′ is compact (IsCompact.cthickening).

5. The test form η. Define η(x) := ζ(x)·(ω(p(x))∘p), i.e. η(x) = ζ(x) • covectorPullback n p (ω(p x)). It is C^∞ (ζ and ω∘p are smooth and pulling back by the fixed linear map p is a continuous linear map on covectors), it has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ ⊆ W′ (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Hence η ∈ D^n(W′).

6. Agreement near spt Z_k. Let N := thickening (δ₀/2) K′ ∪ (W′ ∖ p⁻¹(K)); it is open since K is closed and W′ is open. N ⊇ spt Z_k for every k: if y ∈ spt Z_k, then y ∈ W′ and d(y) ≤ γ; if p(y) ∈ K then y ∈ K′ ⊆ thickening (δ₀/2) K′ (self_subset_thickening), otherwise y ∈ W′ ∖ p⁻¹(K). For x ∈ N, η(x) = ω(p(x))∘p: on thickening (δ₀/2) K′ ⊆ cthickening (δ₀/2) K′ we have ζ(x) = 1; on W′ ∖ p⁻¹(K), p(x) ∉ tsupport ω, so ω(p(x)) = 0 and both sides vanish. Since fderiv ℝ p x = p, step 2(a) gives S′_k(ω) = Z_k(η) for every k.

7. The limit. By hypothesis Z_k(η) → c∫_Q η(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z). For z ∈ Q, η(z)(τ) = ζ(z)·ω(p(z))(pτ_1, …, pτ_n) = ζ(z)·ω(p(z))(e) (compContinuousLinearMap_apply and p(τ_i) = e_i). If p(z) ∈ K then z ∈ K′ (d(z) = 0 ≤ γ), so ζ(z) = 1; otherwise ω(p(z)) = 0. In both cases η(z)(τ) = ω(p(z))(e). Therefore, with ι(a) := Σ_i a_i τ_i,
 ∫_Q η(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) = ∫_Q ω(p(z))(e) dHⁿ(z) (setIntegral_congr_fun on the measurable set Q)
  = ∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(p(ι(a)))(e) da (span_integral (i))
  = ∫_{ℝⁿ} ω(a)(e) da (p∘ι = id)
  = ∫_V ω(a)(e) da (ω = 0 off V: setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
 Hence S′_k(ω) = Z_k(η) → c∫_V ω(a)(e) da = S(ω).

8. Conclusion. Since ω ∈ D^n(V) was arbitrary, S′_k ⇀ S in V. Together with step 2 (each S′_k is integer multiplicity) and step 3, this proves the claim. ∎
